+contract_unknown:
+  - id: contract_unknown.sensei.how_is_a_question_retired_when_nobody_can_ever_answer_it
+    kind: contract_unknown
+    title: How is a question retired when nobody can ever answer it
+    description: 'PR #236 implements the half that can be done honestly: an evidence blocker whose claims are all derived observed claims with fully source-backed premises does not generate a NEW question. The already-open case is left blocking, with a test pinning that behaviour so the gap stays visible rather than being papered over with a status that asserts something untrue.'
+    proposed_contract: 'A generated question whose blocker is later shown to be self-evidenced should reach a terminal state that says WHY it stopped being asked, without asserting it was settled. None of the current dialogue statuses can carry that: superseded requires a superseding question and there is none; answered and resolved claim the question was settled; accepted_unknown is a human accepting a gap, not a generator deciding one. Either the vocabulary gains a withdrawn/unanswerable state whose author is the generator, or retirement stays a human act and the generator may only decline to ask NEW questions.'
+    evidence:
+      - 'globulario/sensei#230 and PR #236 review: suppressing the question only helps tasks that have not asked it yet. A task that already asked keeps an open question nobody can answer, and it keeps blocking closure — which is the downstream case in sensei-code#22.'
+      - 'Attempted the obvious repair and the schema refused it: setting Status=superseded fails validation with ''superseded question requires superseded_by_question''.'
+    domain: github.com/globulario/sensei

+// isHexSHA256 reports whether a digest is present and well-formed, rather than
+// merely declared resolved.
+func isHexSHA256(s string) bool {
+	if len(s) != 64 {
+		return false
+	}
+	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
+		c := s[i]
+		if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

diff --git a/golang/architecture/questiongen/self_evidenced_test.go b/golang/architecture/questiongen/self_evidenced_test.go
index 5939c163..0f275874 100644
--- a/golang/architecture/questiongen/self_evidenced_test.go
+++ b/golang/architecture/questiongen/self_evidenced_test.go
@@ -140,3 +140,74 @@ func generateReport(t *testing.T, ctx Context) (Report, error) {
 	res, err := Generate(ctx, nil)
 	return res.Report, err
 }
+
+// The gap this fix does NOT close, pinned so it stays visible: a question
+// already open for a self-evidenced blocker keeps blocking.
+//
+// Retiring it would be the better answer and cannot be given honestly yet. The
+// dialogue vocabulary has no state for a question withdrawn as unanswerable:
+// `superseded` requires a superseding question and there is none, `answered`
+// and `resolved` would claim it was settled, and `accepted_unknown` is a human
+// accepting a gap rather than a generator deciding one. Filed as a
+// contract_unknown; this test fails the day the vocabulary gains that state,
+// which is the reminder to use it.
+func TestAnAlreadyOpenQuestionStillBlocks(t *testing.T) {
+	// Produce the existing question the way a real earlier run would: the same
+	// blocker, with a premise digest that is not yet resolved, so the question
+	// is generated and schema-valid.
+	first, err := Generate(evidenceCtx(t, func(_ *architecture.Claim, r *architecture.ClaimFactReceipt) {
+		r.Provenance.SourceDigestStatus = architecture.SourceDigestUnavailable
+	}), nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(first.Dialogue.OpenQuestions) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("setup: expected one generated question, got %d", len(first.Dialogue.OpenQuestions))
+	}
+
+	// Now the premise resolves, so the claim carries its own evidence — and the
+	// question asked before is still open.
+	ctx := evidenceCtx(t, nil)
+	ctx.Existing = &first.Dialogue
+	blocker := ctx.Closure.Blockers[0]
+
+	res, err := Generate(ctx, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	covered := false
+	for _, item := range res.Report.ExistingCoverage {
+		if item.BlockerID == blocker.ID {
+			covered = true
+		}
+	}
+	if !covered {
+		t.Fatal("an already-open question is no longer reported as covering its blocker — if it is now retired, this gap is closed and the contract_unknown can be answered")
+	}
+	for _, item := range res.Report.Skipped {
+		if item.Disposition == DispositionSelfEvidenced {
+			t.Fatal("the blocker was reported both covered and suppressed; those cannot both be true")
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// The status is not the evidence. ValidateClaimDocument accepts
+// source_digest_status: resolved with an empty digest, while maintenance reads
+// that as unknown — a receipt claiming resolution without carrying one must not
+// suppress a question.
+func TestAResolvedStatusWithoutADigestDoesNotSuppress(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, digest := range []string{"", "   ", "not-a-digest", strings.Repeat("z", 64)} {
+		ctx := evidenceCtx(t, func(_ *architecture.Claim, r *architecture.ClaimFactReceipt) {
+			r.Provenance.SourceDigest = digest
+		})
+		res, err := Generate(ctx, nil)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		for _, item := range res.Report.Skipped {
+			if item.Disposition == DispositionSelfEvidenced {
+				t.Fatalf("digest %q suppressed a question without carrying evidence", digest)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
